records.name: Denizli
records.summary:
Every province in Türkiye sits under the same intensifying national framework. A leaked draft of the 11th Judicial Package (October 2025) would criminalise LGBT conduct and advocacy — up to 3 years for behaviour 'contrary to biological sex and general morality' and 4 years for same-sex ceremonies — and would raise gender-affirming-care eligibility from 18 to 25 with a permanent-infertility mandate, exposing providers to fines and up to 7 years and patients to up to 3 years; 15 LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected. The Kaos GL 2025 human-rights report ('A Major Siege', published February 2026) finds hostility became explicit state policy in 2025 — presidency-centred, implemented through the family ministry — documenting 6 right-to-life violations including 3 hate-motivated killings with trans people most affected, 89 torture or ill-treatment cases (up from 51) and 313 liberty violations (about 2.5-fold), counted from media coverage because the state keeps no hate-crime statistics.

No province-specific ordinance, incident series or court decision concerning trans visitors in Denizli was documented in this research pass; the national framework above is the whole documented picture for Denizli. The absence of recorded provincial enforcement is not evidence of local tolerance, and equally not evidence of a local ban.

records.name: Diyarbakır
records.summary: Route-3 estimate, now carrying real sub-national evidence: the south-east's largest metropolis, with a conflict-era security legacy (state-of-emergency legacies, village-guard system, high police presence). On 14 September 2024 - the day of a national anti-LGBT "Great Family Gathering" - two men attacked two trans women with sharp objects in the Kayapınar district: Sudenaz Uran was killed at the scene and her friend was injured; the defendants recorded the killing and the recording entered the case file. On 19 December 2025 both were sentenced to aggravated life imprisonment for intentional killing of a woman - the strongest homicide-justice outcome in this country's record - though during the trial the Family and Social Services Ministry's application to intervene was accepted while the local bar association's LGBTI+ commission's was rejected, casting the state as guardian of "the family" rather than of the victim's community. Scored relative to the national score (0.15) for Turkey.
